I turned it into scored targets with these weights:
(1) Pitch height, mid-low (0.20): f0 median 98-118 Hz scores full, falling to zero at 78 and 140 Hz.
(2) Deadpan flatness (0.20): f0 SD 2.8 st or less, declination-removed SD 2.2 st or less, p10-p90 range 8 st or less (zero at 5.0 / 4.0 / 14 st).
(3) Brightness and intelligibility through bitcrush (0.12): centroid 850-1350 Hz, 2-4 kHz presence -21 dB or higher.
(4) Projection, "slightly too loud / clean shouts" (0.10): alpha ratio -10 dB or higher, Hammarberg 22 dB or lower, H1-H2 1 dB or lower (pressed, not breathy).
(5) Light grit on a clean base (0.08): HNR 8.5-12.5 dB, CPPS 7.5 dB or higher. Most of the grit is added in post, so breathy, creaky or velvety voices lose points.
(6) Clipped pace (0.10): 4.3-5.6 syl/s (transcript-based), median syllable-nucleus width 0.18 s or less.
(7) Evenness (0.08): RMS SD 8.5 dB or lower, inter-syllable interval CV 0.40 or lower (weighted by how many nuclei the clip has).
(8) Half-ton size (0.05): apparent vocal tract length 17.8 cm or more.
(9) Style evidence from the preview text (0.07): the robotic, status-report self-description is the highest; whispered, soothing or warm self-descriptions score lowest.
Accent multiplier: Evan x0.6, Knox x0.95.

ranking.name: Leo
ranking.why: He has the best persona and comedy register of all 44, and is the only preset that names both of Oliver's registers. He calls himself "the guy who's actually played the game... casual, a little bit deadpan, and always ready with a punchline... comedy sketches", which is ideal for "...That's THEIR ship." and the one-liner barks, and suits a fan page about a game. His phonation is pressed and clear (H1-H2 -3.4 dB, CPPS 9.1) and his rate is quick (5.0 syl/s), and his p95 of 319 Hz gives real yelp headroom without falsetto.
ranking.risks: He is far above 'mid-range': median 258 Hz, and even his p10 is 196 Hz. That reads teen or boyish, so Oliver could come across as a kid rather than a young-adult soldier. It would also leave no distinct higher voice for Wil, his younger willing-victim friend, and Leo is the obvious Wil. His word-to-word contour mostly stays within ±4 st (deadpan is his default), so the bright, cocky, too-high blurt may not lift enough. A -2 st formant-preserving shift would help, but at the risk of artifacts. His VTL is ceiling-sensitive (5.4 cm spread), so his size cue is uncertain.

ranking.name: Bram
ranking.why: His persona is the audience-hungry show-off. As a self-described faceless-YouTube host ("Stick around, because what happens at the end of this video will completely change how you think", +8.2 st on "Stick"), he fits "the boy requires an audience" and lines like "Is anyone filming this? Somebody should be filming this!" He is bright (centroid 1648 Hz, 2-5 kHz share 0.074) with a brisk 4.9 syl/s, 11.6 st range and p95 296 Hz for yelps. His young-adult VTL (about 16.1-16.3 cm) and plain English also fit.
ranking.risks: He is slightly breathy (H1-H2 5.4 dB, CPPS 6.9). His phrase ends fade and fall (-6 to -8 st at -11 to -15 dB on "sounds", "videos", "think"), which would swallow the payoff words "...Fry?" and "ship" that must land on the hold. His YouTuber-narrator cadence is formulaic and could make Oliver sound like a host rather than a character. At 204 Hz he sits above mid-range. His preview uses a different template (40 kHz WAV with long pauses), so it is less comparable to the others. Laughs and real deadpan are unproven.

picks.name: Orion
picks.why: Both lenses ranked Orion #1, and he stayed #1 under every weighting tried. His preview is already a status report: "Systems online. I am Orion. Data processing complete." It is cut into short phrases with 0.52, 0.86 and 0.84 s silences between them, which is almost exactly C1's 'line, then a half-second dead-still hold'. f0 is 108 Hz, the middle of mid-low. Detrended in-phrase pitch SD is 2.17 st, among the flattest of the speaking voices. He projects more than the other mid-low voices (alpha -9.8 dB, H1-H2 0.9 dB, Hammarberg 23.8), which suits 'slightly too loud' and clean shouts. His rhythm is clipped (5.5 syl/s, 0.15 s nuclei) and his texture is light on a clean base (HNR 9.5, CPPS 9.0). VTL is 18.0 cm, which reads as big. Whisper reads plain English at 0.99, and WER stays at 0 under a heavy bitcrush. The 7.6 s clip makes these the most reliable measures of any B-1000 candidate.
picks.refutation_tried: Against Benji (spec #2): his apparent flatness advantage disappears once the phrase declination is removed. His detrended SD is 2.17 st, the same as Orion's. His lower overall SD comes from having only one calm 2.5 s sentence. He is legato (4.0 syl/s, 0.27 s nuclei), has no pause or hold evidence, and projects softly (alpha -13). Against Callum (casting #2, my runner-up): he does have the line-then-pause cadence and the 'BBG News. Live.' anchor persona. But his newsreader stress peaks reach about 224 Hz (detrended SD 2.78, f0 velocity 35 vs 25 st/s for Orion), he is slightly breathy (CPPS 7.5), and his phonation is softer (alpha -13.6). He also comes from a different 40 kHz stereo template. Pitch can be flattened in post. Timing, clarity and projection can't be added in post, and Orion leads on those. The strongest remaining case against Orion is distinctness. Raw, he sits close to Jasper in timbre (MFCC-stat distance at the 10th percentile of all 946 preset pairs). In my simulation of the bitcrush in post, that rises to the 44th percentile (light crush: 11 kHz hold, 8-bit, 60% wet) and the 83rd (heavy crush: 7.35 kHz, 6-bit). Add the 4 st median gap and his flat contour against Jasper's swoops, and the two stay apart. They also never share a scene in Ep 1. The 'smooth AI narrator' archetype is a style risk, not an imitation: the preset is original and brisk, not the slow, ominous delivery of famous film AIs.
picks.delivery_notes: Text: write every unit as its own sentence ("B one thousand. Live. Scanning location." / "Hazard: crashed dropship." / "Status: still crashed." / "Launch pad destination: the other crashed dropship."). Generate each C1 line as its own clip. In the edit, set every hold to about 0.5 s; his own pauses run 0.5-0.9 s, so trim rather than pad. If he rushes the sign-off at 5.5 syl/s, split "Kill credit: jump pad." / "Assist: Huggables." / "Next location: Steamyard Blues." / "Uploading..." into separate clips, or time-stretch to 92-95%. Leave the natural lift on "Kill credit" unflattened. Never add style words that steer him toward a famous film robot or a slow, ominous AI read. Post chain, in order: (1) formant-preserving pitch-variance reduction of about 50-70% around each line's median, keeping the final fall so the periods land; (2) light drive or saturation for half-ton weight; (3) bitcrush, sample-and-hold at about 11 kHz and 8-bit at around 60% wet for dialogue, heavier on shouts, with no vocoder or ring-mod; (4) sit him 2-3 dB above the dialogue bus. "Tee-hee.": generate as its own clip in 3-4 takes ("Tee-hee!", "Tee-hee.", "Hee-hee!"). If he reads it flat, pitch it up 3-5 st with formants preserved. Give it a lighter crush so it reads bright, then hard cut.

picks.name: Jasper
picks.why: Jasper is the spec lens's #1 under all six weightings, and the casting lens's own pick if there is no regional accent. Core f0 is 94.5 Hz (raw median 83 Hz, pulled down by phrase-final fry), a real baritone. He has the warmest spectrum of any credible baritone (centroid 679 Hz, body share 0.76) and natural gravel (HNR 10.3, CPPS 8.5, half-harmonics -20.8 dB, fry at phrase ends). He is the most expressive low voice in the set (SD 5.3 st, p10-p90 range 13.4 st) with the largest upper reach of any baritone (13.6 st). His one line swoops from 182 Hz down to 66 Hz, an operatic arc that covers the grand C3, the lift on "look", the resigned "...Mayday." and a future native squeak "D'oh!". His pace is slow (3.7 syl/s), so lines stay under 3 s with room for the pause. VTL is 18.4 cm, accent neutral (p_en 0.99). He was #2 on the old shortlist and is in the reel Bryce received. Post can add presence and grain. It cannot add range, warmth or tract size, and Jasper leads on all three.
picks.refutation_tried: Against Sterling (casting #1): his persona text ('warm, resonant, intimate and epic') is the closest match, but three things count against him. (1) His self-stated Southern accent, confirmed partly non-rhotic by the F3 probe, is neither the wiki's Spanish accent nor neutral. Open item 13 only asks 'Spanish accent or none', so he would add a regional identity nobody asked for. A Southern 'getcha' next to "Ay, dios mio!" would make the accent part of the joke, which the soul forbids. (2) He measures fast (5.7 syl/s) against 'slow, solemn'. (3) He has the narrowest range of the baritones (SD 3.3 st, p90 118 Hz, +6.4 st reach), which is thin for operatic melodrama. Alistair is RP and cool, 'whispered', so he is also off-spec. Against Fraser (my runner-up, the neutral alternative): he is the real threat. He projects more (alpha -9.3 vs -15.7 dB, modal H1-H2 0 vs 3.5 dB), has the biggest tract (19.4 cm, ceiling-sensitive) and a solemn suspense read, so 'Home.' may come out chestier. But his expressiveness is moderate (SD 3.5, +6.7 st reach), and his clip is even shorter (2.2 s). Raw, he also sits closer to Orion than Jasper does (LTAS distance at the 1st percentile vs Jasper's 15th; after a light crush, 23rd vs 44th). Jasper's weaknesses are the darkest presence of all 44 (2-4 kHz -23.9 dB) and a soft, slightly breathy source. Both can be fixed in post. Fraser's missing range can't. Jasper wins, but on a 2.7 s wistful clip.
picks.delivery_notes: Use one clip per line and keep each under 3 s. C2: "Oliver, we'll getcha... home." Keep the ellipsis. If seed_audio doesn't leave about 0.5 s before "home", cut it in the edit (his one allowed pause). C3: generate "This arm, I did not ask for." and "But look at it." separately. If "look" doesn't lift, try "But LOOK at it." for a second take. C4: "Home." is the risky line, because his preview ends in fry at 66-69 Hz. Run 3 takes ("Home.", "Home!", "Home...!") and pick the one with the most chest and the least creak; a formant-preserving +1 st on the tail is acceptable. C5: "...Mayday." Here the fry helps. Pick the smallest, most resigned take, pull it down about 6 dB, and leave the 0.5 s silence before it. Post: +2-3 dB presence bell near 3 kHz and a gentle low cut below 70 Hz so the darkest preview of the 44 cuts through the brass cue. Add light tape or tube saturation only if the gravel disappears in the generated takes. No bitcrush. Spanish phrases, when they come, are spoken plainly, with no put-on accent. The future "D'oh!" is his own squeak; try it natively first (13.6 st reach) and pitch it up only if needed, never in imitation of the famous cartoon one.

picks.name: John
picks.why: John meets the casting note ('bright, mid-range young-adult, a grin in it, bravado cracking into a yelp') on the most reliable evidence: a 17 s clip. He is bright (alpha -3.6 dB, centroid 1428 Hz, top-20% presence) and very clean (CPPS 14.3, HNR 14.9, creak 0.016), so the grin and the crack come from the raw voice, as they must, since Oliver gets no bitcrush. f0 is 174 Hz with p95 260 Hz, enough yelp headroom. VTL 17.5 cm reads as young adult. His preview is cocky self-praise with a grin ('Hey, yay! The name's John!... That's where I shine, baby.'), which is Oliver's 'Woohoo! Way to go, me!' engine. On exclamation marks he lifts +7 to +8 st ("yay!", "John!"), and C2 is three exclamations in a row. His in-phrase flatness (2.47 st, the flattest of the Oliver candidates) suggests he can play the C4 deadpan. He is also the most distinct candidate from the chosen Sanchez: f0 overlap with Jasper 0.20 (22nd percentile of all pairs), timbre distance 80th percentile, LTAS 84th percentile, and only 2% of his voiced frames at or below 110 Hz.
picks.refutation_tried: Against Andre (casting #1, spec #2): he has the swagger text and the widest range, but he fails 'bright' (alpha -10.4, centroid 1081). More decisively, he collides with Sanchez. 37% of his voiced frames sit at or below 110 Hz and 29% at or below 100 Hz, because his phrase ends drop into fry at 80-89 Hz. His f0 overlap with Jasper is 0.52 (59th percentile) and his timbre distance only the 16th percentile, so in the C4 exchange ("Home." / "...That's THEIR ship.") his deadpan drop would land in Jasper's register. He is also the closest timbre to Orion (LTAS at the 0th percentile). Against Dylan (my runner-up): the two lenses average to an exact tie (7.95 each). Dylan is the most literal 'mid-range' (151 Hz) and his 'proudly ... muddy shoe' line has a smiling lift-and-deflate, but the only evidence is one neutral 3 s sentence, with no attitude, laugh or deadpan shown and a rougher short-clip voice (HNR 9.3, shimmer 13.6%). John breaks the tie on proven attitude and on distinctness from Sanchez. The case against John that I could not dismiss: he describes himself as 'a little nasal' and 'quirky sidekick, oddball villain', which could make Oliver whiny or goofy rather than a cocky lead with a cool-guy veneer. At 174 Hz he sits at the top of 'mid-range' and closer to a future Wil. This is why the pick needs an audition.
picks.delivery_notes: C2: generate "Sanchez! Buddy! You look GREAT!" as one clip and "...Fry?" as another. Put a half-beat (about 0.3 s) of silence between them in the edit so "Fry?" lands on the hold. For the full mouth, low-pass the C2 clips around 3-4 kHz and add soft mouth noise. If he isn't 'too high' enough, apply +1-2 st with formants preserved. C4: "...That's THEIR ship." Use a period, no exclamation, and run 3-4 takes. If no single take is both flat and cracking, splice a flat take with a "THEIR" from a take that breaks upward (+2-3 st). Never prompt for a 'funny voice' or a cartoon character; the lines carry the comedy. Post: he is already bright, so add no presence boost. If the nasality reads as whiny, cut 2-3 dB around 1-1.5 kHz. Keep his level slightly under Sanchez's in the two-handers so the grin doesn't turn shrill.

decision.distinctness: The three leads sit roughly an octave apart top to bottom, and each has its own contour and treatment. Pitch: Sanchez (Jasper) has a raw median of 83 Hz and a core of about 95 Hz. B-1000 (Orion) is 108 Hz, +4.0 st above Jasper. Oliver (John) is 174 Hz, +8.3 st above Orion and +12.4 st above Jasper. Contour: B-1000 is flat and clipped, with his pitch variance reduced in post. Sanchez is operatic, swooping from 182 Hz down to 66 Hz. Oliver is bouncy and bright, lifting 7-8 st on exclamations. Timbre: I equalised bandwidth (everything low-passed at 7 kHz), took MFCC statistics and 1/3-octave LTAS, and ranked each pair against all 946 preset pairs. Ep 1's only on-screen pair, Jasper and John (C2-C4), is the most separated of every finalist pair: f0 overlap 0.20 (22nd percentile), timbre 80th percentile, LTAS 84th percentile. Orion and John are also well apart (f0 overlap 0.24, timbre 62nd percentile). The one close pair raw is Orion and Jasper (timbre 10th percentile). With B-1000's bitcrush simulated, their distance rises to the 44th percentile with a light crush (11 kHz / 8-bit / 60% wet) and the 83rd with a heavy crush (7.35 kHz / 6-bit). Combined with the flat-versus-swooping contours, the 4 st gap and the very different personas (sincere machine log versus melodramatic hero), that keeps them apart. In Ep 1 they never share a scene: C1 and the sign-off are B-1000 alone. For later shorts where they meet, keep B-1000's crush at medium or heavier, not the lightest setting. Andre was rejected partly because he would have blurred both edges: 29% of his voiced frames sit at or below 100 Hz in Sanchez's range, and his LTAS is the closest to Orion's. No voice is used twice. feature_notes:
The file is a JSON list with one record for each of the 44 male presets. All voice_ids match male_voices.tsv and no core field is null.

Scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-thallo-site/91c60972-6d3f-51de-9a92-c1d563bcf5a4/scratchpad/voices_tools/:
- features_v2.py (args: tsv, audio_dir, transcripts, whisper_models, out)
- diag_octave.py (octave, noise-floor and formant-ceiling checks)
- features_v2_run.log

METHOD
- Loading: librosa at the native rate, downmixed to mono. Resampled to 22.05 kHz for Praat (parselmouth 0.4.7 / Praat 6.1.38) and to 16 kHz for spectral measures and Whisper. Clip durations come from librosa; soundfile's header durations were wrong for some MP3s.
- f0: Praat autocorrelation, two passes (Hirst): 50-600 Hz, then floor = 0.72*q35 and ceiling = 1.9*q65. Fields: f0_median_hz, f0_p10_hz, f0_p90_hz, the p10-p90 range in semitones, and f0_semitone_sd.
- Speaking rate: De Jong & Wempe (2009) syllable nuclei, rebuilt on arrays. Intensity peaks above (99th percentile - 25 dB), a dip of more than 2 dB, and a voiced frame inside the sounding parts of Praat's silence detection (pauses of 0.3 s or more removed). Fields: articulation_rate_nuclei_per_s, and a cross-check articulation_rate_transcript_syl_per_s (transcript syllables from a heuristic counter, divided by the same speech time).
- HNR: Praat cross-correlation harmonicity mean.
- Jitter and shimmer (local, %): Praat point process with the standard 0.0001/0.02/1.3/1.6 settings.
- Formants: primary values from Praat FormantPath, which picks a ceiling per frame between about 4.1 and 6.1 kHz around 5 kHz. F1-F4 are medians over voiced frames.
- Apparent VTL: c/(2*dF), with c = 35000 cm/s and dF from a least-squares fit through the origin, Fi = (2i-1)/2*dF (Reby & McComb). Also given: an F3/F4-only VTL, the fixed-5 kHz F1-F4 and VTL, and vtl_ceiling_spread_cm (the VTL spread across fixed 4.5/5.0/5.5 kHz ceilings) as a reliability measure.
- Spectral (0-8 kHz on every clip, so codec bandwidth doesn't bias it): magnitude-weighted centroid median, flatness, LTAS tilt (dB/octave from 100 to 7500 Hz), alpha ratio, and power_share_below_300hz.
- RMS dynamics: SD in dB of 30 ms frame RMS within the sounding spans, plus the p10-p90 range.
- Accent hint: faster-whisper small detect_language on the first 30 s, averaged over three versions of the clip (as-is, silence-trimmed, peak-normalised with padding). Fields: top-3 languages, p_en and its range across the three, and the top non-English language.
- Transcript fields: self_description, stated_accent, stated_style, verbatim style_quotes and the full transcript. accent_hint is a one-line summary and flags lists the reliability notes.

SANITY CHECKS
- f0 agrees with the old pyin analysis for most voices. Old outliers are fixed: Archie went from 165 to 132 Hz, and the old 9.0 st SD was octave jumps. Kevin is now 131 Hz and Alexey 106 Hz; the old 60 Hz floor clamped Vlad.
- The high voices are real, not octave errors. On Leo 258, Cody 242, Bram 204, Miles 202, Evan 180, John 174 and Reid 170 Hz, energy at the half-harmonics is 24-35 dB below the harmonics, and Praat cc and SHS agree.
- Vlad (54 Hz) and Gideon (66 Hz) really are very low; their odd harmonics are present.
- The first run used a power-weighted centroid, giving Caspian 88 Hz. It is now magnitude-weighted, median 978 Hz, matching the old analysis.
- Gideon's VTL with a fixed 5 kHz ceiling was 14.8 cm, which contradicts "deep". FormantPath gives 18.4 cm (F3/F4-only also 18.4).
- Vlad's transcript syllable count (55) matches a hand count. His rate is about 2.4 syl/s, the slowest of the set.
- The two speaking-rate measures correlate at r = 0.64. Nuclei undercount by about 9% on average and badly on some 2 s clips (Holden: 5 nuclei for 9 to 10 syllables). Treat the transcript-based rate as the more reliable one.
- The long gaps in Callum and Marcus are real silences (dramatic pauses and a long silent tail), so their speech time is correct.

ACCENT FINDINGS
- Evan: the only strong non-native cue. Catalan about 0.84, Spanish about 0.10, English about 0.03, stable across all three versions. Whisper's free transcription of the English sentence is still correct, so read this as Spanish/Catalan-accented English.
- Knox: mild Welsh mass (cy about 0.09, p_en 0.85), possibly a British/Welsh flavour.
- Cody and Caspian: small non-English mass, about 0.02-0.04.
- Whisper-small does not pick up native regional accents. The self-described British (Arthur), Irish (Cillian), Southern (Sterling) and middle-American (Brooks) voices all read about 0.99 English, so use stated_accent for those.
- Alexey and Vlad show no detectable Eastern-European cue despite their names.

CAVEATS
- 23 voices have less than 4 s of speech (single-sentence previews), so their jitter, shimmer and formant medians are noisy and depend on which vowels the sentence happens to use.
- Jitter (1.5-4.2%) and shimmer (5.7-14%) come from connected TTS speech through a codec, so compare them between voices only, never against clinical norms.
- Ceiling-sensitive formants (spread over 2.5 cm, flagged): Leo, Gideon, Evan, Vlad, Cody, Caspian, Fraser, Ian, Barrett, Alden, Sterling, Desmond, Landon.
- Caspian has about 95% of its power below 300 Hz (heavy bass EQ), so its centroid and formants are untrustworthy.
- Barrett and Evan come out at about 15 cm VTL (a small or bright tract) with every method.
- John and Orion are band-limited to about 11 kHz at source; the 0-8 kHz spectral stats are still comparable.
- Callum, Bram and Marcus are a different preview template (40 kHz stereo WAV with long pauses).
- Previews show timbre and the preset's intended style, not how a voice will deliver our lines.
